summary: Iteration 19 — frontend-only verification at 390x844 of (1) SHARE-INTO-APOLLO landing via URL params and (2) INCIDENT TIMELINE + Home Threat Scent card + Event-detail incident link + regression smoke. SHARE landing: all 4 classifications (link/email/account/message) render correct share-kind label ('Looks like a link' / 'an email' / 'an account or login alert' / 'a text message or chat'), correct share-go button label ('Check as …'), and navigate correctly to /check?url=… (link) with source=share, /email with email-body prefilled (email — email-run then triggers Barking state with scenario shown), /account?text=…&source=share with account-text prefilled to 'Microsoft: Approve this sign-in request? If this wasn't you, deny.', and /message with the parcel text prefilled. share-alt-* buttons are present for message-payload cases (share-alt-link, share-alt-email, share-alt-account visible on the parcel/message case; tapping share-alt-email correctly opens /email with body prefilled and 'parcel' text preserved). INCIDENT TIMELINE: after building the chain message('CommBank …locked… commbank-secure-verify.top/login') → account (mfa_prompt / bank / initiated-no / run) → Home shows exactly one 'Connected events (Threat Scent)' card (testID prefix home-scent-<uuid>) with pills 'Barking', 'CommBank', '2 events' — tap opens /patrol/scent/<id> with testIDs incident-state='Barking', incident-count='2 connected events', incident-headline='CommBank impersonation — message → account alert', incident-event-0 (💬 Message, at earlier time) & incident-event-1 (🔐 Account alert, at later time) rendered in time order, incident-plan renders 4 generic steps (progress '0/4' → tap incident-step-0 → '1/4' with strike-through), incident-ask present, incident-resolve fires the toast 'Incident marked handled. Apollo keeps the record.' EVENT-DETAIL: patrol tab lists both events (testID prefix patrol-item-<id>); opening the account event renders event-title 'Account: Fake CommBank security alert — My bank' with event-incident-card and event-incident-open visible; tapping event-incident-open navigates to the same /patrol/scent/<id> timeline. REGRESSION SMOKE: /file opens without auto-analysis and exposes file-source-*, file-pw, file-pick, file-name-check testIDs (no file-run triggered); /email, /account, /network open and close cleanly (all return to /home); /message renders sender+text inputs. ONE CRITICAL BUG FOUND — incident-resolve only marks 1 of the 2 linked events as resolved (the LATER-processed one gets overwritten by the stale-closure); consequently the 'incident-handled' pill never appears and one of the two events still shows 'Barking' in Patrol. Full RCA and repro in rca_of_issue. NOTE (spec deviation on link-only share): the spec expects 'share-alt-message present (no share-alt-link)' on /share?url=… but the current alternativeRoutes implementation returns NO alternatives when only a webUrl (and no free text) is shared, because the message/email/account alternatives are gated behind `if (raw)` where raw='' — so no share-alt-* buttons render for the URL-only case. This may or may not be intentional; flagged as a design decision to reconcile with the spec.

ui_bugs.issue: Tapping incident-resolve only marks the LAST-iterated linked event as resolved. resolveAll iterates `linked` sequentially, awaiting resolveEvent(e), but resolveEvent → upsertEvent captures `events` via useCallback dep at render time. Between the two iterations React state has not re-rendered, so both calls execute against the SAME stale `events` snapshot. The second upsertEvent rebuilds `next = [e2-resolved, ...events.filter(x => x.event_id !== e2)]` which re-includes e1 in its ORIGINAL active state, overwriting the just-persisted resolved status of e1. Net effect: only 1 of N events becomes resolved (event-0 in the timeline order I observed), plan.allResolved stays false → 'incident-handled' pill never renders, and the still-active event continues to show 'Barking' in Patrol. Reference: /app/frontend/app/patrol/scent/[id].tsx:49 and /app/frontend/src/store/ApolloContext.tsx:272-288, 430-433.

When only ?url=… is shared (no free text), alternativeRoutes returns [] because message/email/account alternatives are gated behind `if (raw)` and raw is ''. Spec expects share-alt-message to still be present for URL-only shares. Reference: /app/frontend/src/share/classifyShare.ts:49-52.

integration_issues.issue: Because only one event gets persisted as resolved (see resolveAll bug), the Patrol tab still shows the OTHER linked event as 'Barking' / active after the user taps 'I've done the steps — mark incident handled', despite the toast claiming success.

action_items: CRITICAL — fix stale-closure in /app/frontend/app/patrol/scent/[id].tsx `resolveAll`. Options: (a) call resolveEvent with the already-updated event by reading from the latest events state inside a functional setState / a ref; or better (b) add a batch API on ApolloContext like `resolveEvents(events: PatrolEvent[])` that computes ONE next array with all resolutions applied and calls persistEvents once; or (c) change upsertEvent to use functional setEvents(prev => …) so back-to-back awaited calls each see the previous prev. This bug also affects any other place that performs a loop of awaited upsertEvent calls (mark-safe on multiple events, etc.).

MEDIUM — reconcile /share?url=… alternatives: either make alternativeRoutes also emit message/email/account choices when only a webUrl is present (spec expects share-alt-message on the URL-only case) OR update the spec/test. Suggested fix in classifyShare.ts:49-52: always emit message/email/account routes from `raw || url` so the user can re-check a bare URL as a message/email/account snippet.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/store/ApolloContext.tsx:272-288 — upsertEvent closes over `events`. Any caller that awaits it more than once in a synchronous burst (e.g., resolveAll, bulk trust flows) will operate on stale state. Convert to functional updates: `setEvents(prev => ...)` inside persistEvents, plus keep a ref of events for the storage write. Alternatively expose a bulk `upsertEvents(inputs: PatrolEvent[])`.

/app/frontend/app/patrol/scent/[id].tsx:49 — resolveAll shows the success toast unconditionally even if only one event was actually resolved. After the fix above, keep the guard `plan.allResolved` before showing 'Incident marked handled'.

success_rate.frontend: SHARE 4/4 kinds classify+navigate correctly; incident-timeline UI 100% renders correctly; resolve action FAILS to mark all events (1/2 resolved) → 1 CRITICAL bug; URL-only share-alt spec mismatch → 1 MEDIUM bug; regression smoke 6/6 pass

seed_data_creation: None persisted. Fresh browser session each run; onboarding via onboarding-start-button → disclosure-accept-button. The Threat Scent chain is rebuilt inside the test by /message + /account.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To reproduce the incident-resolve bug: (1) onboarding-start-button → disclosure-accept-button, (2) /message: sender='CommBank', text='CommBank: your account is locked. Verify now at https://commbank-secure-verify.top/login', message-check (state Barking), (3) message-check-account → account-kind-mfa_prompt → account-provider-bank → account-initiated-no → account-run (state Barking, account-linked shown), (4) close modals → /(tabs)/home shows home-scent-<id> pill '2 events', (5) tap → /patrol/scent/<id>. Toggle incident-step-0 to see progress '0/4' → '1/4'. Tap incident-resolve → toast fires but ONLY the second incident-event- becomes 'Handled' in Patrol; the incident-handled pill never appears because plan.allResolved is false. To validate the fix, after tapping incident-resolve BOTH incident-event-0 and incident-event-1 must show the 'Handled' pill AND the top summary must render the 'Handled' pill (testID incident-handled), AND on the Patrol tab both patrol-item-* rows must display 'Handled' rather than 'Barking'.
rca_of_issue: STALE-CLOSURE in resolveAll (patrol/scent/[id].tsx:49) → upsertEvent (ApolloContext.tsx:272-288). resolveAll = `for (const e of linked) if (e.status === 'active') await resolveEvent(e); showToast(...);`. resolveEvent → upsertEvent({...e, status:'resolved'}). upsertEvent has deps [events, ...] so it's re-created each render, but during a synchronous JS tick React batches state updates: the setEvents inside persistEvents does not force upsertEvent to be re-created before the NEXT await resolves in the same task queue. The result: both awaited calls run through the SAME closure whose `events` snapshot is the pre-resolve list. Second call's `next = [e2-resolved, ...events.filter(x => x.event_id !== e2.event_id)]` re-inserts e1 with its ORIGINAL active status, silently overwriting the successful first persist. Because `linked` is ordered by insertion (events prepends newest → linked = [account, message] in my run), the LOOP processes account first (its resolution gets overwritten) then message (which sticks). Timeline sorts by occurred_at asc, so timeline[0] = message (Handled ✓), timeline[1] = account (still Barking ✗). Mitigation options in action_items.
